spans.text: "The strong do what they can, and the weak suffer what they must."
—Thucydides, The History of the Peloponnesian War.
"Terminus" Laboratory, Stasi Building Underground, Frankfurt, White Zone.

Inside the cramped operating room, a young man stands before the surgical table. His hands are clasped together. With slow, measured breaths, he steadies the restless pounding of his heart in a state of feigned rest.
Father... the instruments have been counted. Please double check them.
He opens his eyes.

Facing the deferential white-clad Nyto, William does something unprecedented—he smiles. At this moment, his spirits have risen to their highest point in years. Even the trash before him seems almost tolerable.
The instruments are correct.
...Wonderful.
Vital signs are stable. Anesthetic metabolism is estimated to complete in seven minutes.
We're close now. Success is within reach.
Father...
BOOM!!!
...My sisters report that Griffin's forces are almost here.
You're not needed here anymore. Get out.
Yes, Father.
Another explosion detonates above after the Nyto departs, and even the operating room trembles.
The roar of battle draws closer and closer. Five minutes remain.
Ignoring the relentless blasts and violent shaking, William takes a seat. He reaches out and takes Lunasia's hand—the hand of the one he loves most.
Amid a world boiling in chaos, she is his final salvation.
It is enough. He has done it. Everything is complete. Now all that remains is to wait.
While he waits, he is suddenly struck by a curious question—when was the last time he had experienced such exhilaration, such buoyant elation that even the ugliness of the world seemed diminished?
The memory is hazy. But without question, these days in Frankfurt have been the happiest of his life.
...The great Oberstein—that severe, ambitious overlord—has suffered a fate as pitiful as a stray dog dying by the roadside.
And this is far from over. I will tear down everything he built, piece by piece.
What he once inflicted upon you will return upon all that he held dear—tenfold, a hundredfold...
And that nagging, self-righteous old hag—that pathetic creature, forever chasing the shadow of the dead.
Did she truly believe she could control you and lecture me? It's like an insect presuming to teach an eagle how to soar...
...We have come such a long way, haven't we, Sister?
Lunasia's eyelids twitch.
But even the smallest sign does not escape William's notice.
A sign that she's awakening.
I swore I would bring us back together. I swore that the real you would return to this world.
In the new world beyond the shore, we will remain together forever... as family.
The explosions grow nearer, the thunder of destruction deafening even through the sealed operating room.
A stone pillar crashes down beside him, shattering against the floor, but he seems utterly unfazed. He does not even spare it a glance.
All of his attention is fixed on his sister.
Her breathing grows steadier. The movement of her eyes becomes more frequent.
The future he has long envisioned now lies within his grasp.
The goddess is about to descend upon this old world, steeped in suffering.
Five...
Gunfire erupts again.
Four...
Trash clashes with trash; the ringing of metal against metal forms a savage rhythm.
Three...
Flames roar, like sacred fire burning away decay to herald rebirth.
Two...
The pounding of a heart is clear as thunder; the overturning of reality is but an instant away.
One...
—BOOM!!!
The explosion detonates at point-blank range. He does not waver in the slightest.
His gaze is captured by those holy eyes. Nothing else matters anymore.
In that instant, the world comes to a halt.
...The future is here.
